item.title: On Parallel Sums of Set-Valued Operators: Monotonicity, Paramonotonicity, and Decomposition Invariance
item.description: arXiv:2611.05523v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate structural properties of the parallel sum of set-valued operators in a real Hilbert space, with particular emphasis on monotonicity, maximal monotonicity, and paramonotonicity. We examine the decomposition-invariance property of the parallel sum of two paramonotone operators and provide a direct proof based on monotonicity and the equality of admissible decompositions. This approach establishes the required orthogonality relations without invoking the Attouch--Th{\'e}ra Duality duality framework. We also revisit the classical maximal-monotonicity property of the parallel sum and present an alternative graph-based derivation involving an auxiliary shifted operator. Furthermore, we study the parallel sum of a set-valued operator and the normal cone operator associated with a closed linear subspace. Explicit characterizations of its values, domain, and range are presented, and a decomposition-independent representation is obtained under paramonotonicity through the orthogonality of the underlying subspaces. These results provide a unified and self-contained treatment of selected properties of parallel sums and clarify the role of paramonotonicity in their structural behavior.
item.dc:creator: Salihah Thabet Alwadani

item.title: Calder\'{o}n's complex interpolations of variable-exponent Fofana spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.05628v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fofana spaces, introduced in the framework of Wiener amalgam spaces, can be viewed as generalizations of Morrey spaces. These spaces have attracted considerable attention in recent years and have found applications in the study of partial differential equations. In this paper, we investigate their variable-exponent counterparts. More specifically, we describe Calder\'{o}n's, first and second, complex interpolations of Fofana spaces with variable exponent, as well as the corresponding interpolation spaces of their preduals. Our results recover, as special cases, those already known for (classical) Fofana and Morrey spaces.
item.dc:creator: Nouffou Diarra, Pokou Nagacy, Sekou Coulibaly

item.title: Linear Cotype Bounds for Nonlinear Spectral Gaps of Scalar Expanders
item.description: arXiv:2611.05649v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a finite simple $d$-regular graph, $d\geq 3$, whose second largest adjacency eigenvalue satisfies $\lambda_2(G)\leq (1-\delta)d$, where $0<\delta\leq 1$. We prove that the Poincar\'e constant satisfies $$\gamma(G,\|\cdot\|_X)\lesssim \frac{qCK}{\delta}$$ whenever $X$ is a real Banach space with a $K$-unconditional Schauder basis and cotype $q$ with constant $C$. This constant compares the mean distance over all vertex pairs with the mean distance across edges. For real Banach lattices the bound is $O(qC/\delta)$. The proof estimates where a random walk first leaves each coordinate level set. As a consequence of the bound, if $n$-vertex graphs in a fixed-degree expander family embed with bounded distortion into spaces with bounded $C,K$, then $q$ must grow at least as fast as $\log n$. This order is attained in $\ell_q^n$.
item.dc:creator: Achintya Raya Polavarapu

item.title: BMV conjecture and positivity of spectral shift for relatively Schatten perturbations
item.description: arXiv:2611.05879v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish BMV-type results and prove the positivity-preserving property and uniqueness of support-normalized spectral shift functions of arbitrary order for semibounded operators with relatively Schatten-von Neumann perturbations. We also derive correlation inequalities in the relative Hilbert-Schmidt case. These results build on a new positivity-preserving property for the trace of a higher-order operator derivative along a relatively Schatten direction and are obtained using methods of multilinear operator integration and approximation.
item.dc:creator: Chandan Pradhan, Anna Skripka

item.title: Empirical approximation of $L^p$ norms for $p\in (1, 2)$
item.description: arXiv:2611.05930v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $p\in[1,2]$, we prove uniform moment estimates for weighted sums \[ \sum_{j=1}^m\zeta_jw_j|\langle{\bf v}_j,y\rangle|^p \] of independent subgaussian random variables $\zeta_j$, where the unit vectors $\{{\bf v}_j\}_{j=1}^m$ and nonnegative weights $\{w_j\}_{j=1}^m$ form an isotropic frame. This allows us to obtain optimal sampling discretization of $L_p$ norms for each fixed $p\in[1,2]$. Namely, for an $N$-dimensional space $X_N$ of bounded functions satisfying $\|f\|_\infty\le\sqrt {KN}\,\|f\|_{L_2}$ for every $f\in X_N$, we show that $m\ge C\varepsilon^{-2}KN\log(2N)$ independent samples $\xi^1,\ldots,\xi^m$ provide the discretization \[ (1-\varepsilon)\|f\|_{L_p}^p \le\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m|f(\xi^j)|^p \le(1+\varepsilon)\|f\|_{L_p}^p \quad\forall f\in X_N \] with probability at least $1-\exp(-c\frac{m\varepsilon^2}{KN})$. This implies a corresponding weighted discretization result that, for $1<p<2$, improves Talagrand's bound on the dimension $m$ needed to embed $N$-dimensional subspaces of $L_p$ into $\ell_p^m$ with distortion at most $1+\varepsilon$, giving $m\le C\varepsilon^{-2}N\log(2N)$.
item.dc:creator: Feng Dai, Egor Kosov

item.title: Parabolic Extrapolation of Compactness with Applications to Characterizations of the Parabolic CMO Space via Parabolic Fractional Commutators
item.description: arXiv:2611.05933v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we prove two compactness parabolic extrapolation theorems for linear operators and their commutators on parabolic weighted Lebesgue spaces. As applications, we show that $b\in\mathrm{PCMO}$ (parabolic CMO space) if and only if $b\in L_\mathrm{loc}^1$ and the commutator $[b,I_\alpha^{\gamma+}]_k$ is compact from $L^r(\omega^r)$ to $L^q(\omega^q)$ for any $k\in\mathbb{N}$, $1<r<q<\infty$ with $\frac{1}{r}-\frac{1}{q}=\alpha\in(0,1)$, and $\omega\in A_{r,q}^+(\gamma)$ (parabolic Muckenhoupt class), where $I_\alpha^{\gamma+}$ is the parabolic fractional integral. Several other equivalent characterizations of the space $\mathrm{PCMO}$ are also given. Our approach combines the unweighted compactness for mixed commutators, a local lower estimate for $[b,I_\alpha^{\gamma+}]_k$, and both a quantitative Uchiyama-type description and the equivalence with $\inf_T\{\|[\cdot,I_\alpha^{\gamma+}]_k-T\|_{L^r\to L^q}^\frac{1}{k}\}$ of $\mathrm{dist}_{\mathrm{PBMO}}(\cdot,\mathrm{PCMO})$, where the infimum is taken over all compact operators $T:L^r\to L^q$. Finally, we establish two parabolic weighted Fr\'echet--Kolmogorov compactness criteria, which further induce a parabolic interpolation theorem of compactness.
item.dc:creator: Mingming Cao, Weiyi Kong, Dachun Yang, Wen Yuan, Chenfeng Zhu

item.title: Descriptor representations of geometric port-Hamiltonian systems on Hilbert spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.06080v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish conversions in both directions between geometric and descriptor representations of linear port-Hamiltonian systems on infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces. For the geometric-to-descriptor conversion, we represent the possibly multivalued inverse Dirac relation by a skew-adjoint operator on enlarged Hilbert spaces, retaining the original operator-domain restrictions. The construction accommodates internal and external ports. We show that the conversions preserve trajectories and the power balance. An incompressible Kelvin--Voigt solid illustrates the results.
item.dc:creator: Anna Fischer, Timo Reis

item.title: Linear maps of $C^*$-algebras preserving norm parallelism
item.description: arXiv:2611.06187v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two elements $a,b$ in a normed space are parallel if $\|a+\gamma b\|=\|a\|+\|b\|$ for some $|\gamma|=1$; they form a triangle equality attaining (TEA) pair if $\|a+b\|=\|a\|+\|b\|$. For finite-dimensional complex $C^*$-algebras other than $\mathbf M_2(\mathbb C)$ and $\mathbb C\oplus_\infty\mathbb C$, bijective linear maps on these algebras preserving parallel or TEA pairs are scalar multiples of isometries. For unital abelian algebras with spectra containing at least three points, preservation in both directions gives the same conclusion. We obtain corresponding results for type I factors, simple type I $C^*$-algebras, and unitarily invariant operator spaces under additional continuity and finite-rank hypotheses. All results for $C(X)$ and $B(H,K)$ hold over both real and complex fields.
item.dc:creator: Chi-Kwong Li, Ming-Cheng Tsai, Ya-Shu Wang, Ngai-Ching Wong

item.title: Quasi-norms on $\mathbb{R}^d$: Characterization and Approximation by Conic Splines
item.description: arXiv:2611.06212v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We first show that a regularizer on $\mathbb{R}^d$ that is continuous, symmetric, and amplitude-equivariant is of the form $g=q^\gamma$ with $\gamma>0$, where $q$ is continuous and absolutely homogeneous; we call the set of such $q$ the CH class, whose convex members are the seminorms. Within the CH class, we single out two configurations of interest for regularization: the quasi-norms, which are exactly the positive-definite members of the family, and the quasi-seminorms with null space control, which are the composition of a quasi-norm with a linear map that sets the null space. We then propose a universal parametrization of the class by conic splines, the continuous functions that are linear on each cone of a polyhedral fan. Specifically, we show that the polyhedral CH functionals are exactly the symmetric non-negative conic splines, and that these admit a stable nodal representation in a basis of conic B-splines. Finally, we determine the rates of approximation: the conic spline interpolant converges at the second-order rate $h^2\asymp n^{-2/(d-1)}$, in the $L_\infty$-norm on the hyper-sphere when the angular profile is twice differentiable, and in the $L_1$-norm when its spherical Hessian variation is bounded, which covers the polyhedral members of the class. The rate is sharp, already for the Euclidean norm. The planar case is worked out in full, with the trigonometric hat functions as basis and an $\ell_1$-norm of second differences as regularity index.
item.dc:creator: Michael Unser

item.title: Endpoint Schatten class properties of commutators on quantum Euclidean spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.06405v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study commutators $[(-\Delta_\theta)^{\frac{\epsilon}{2}},M_x]$ involving fractional Laplacians on quantum Euclidean spaces associated with arbitrary real antisymmetric matrices $\theta$. For $d\geq2$ and $-\frac d2<\epsilon\neq 0<1$, we characterize critical weak Schatten class membership of $[(-\Delta_\theta)^{\frac{\epsilon}{2}},M_x]$ for any $x$ as a tempered distribution by Sobolev spaces, with equivalent corresponding norms. We also establish precise asymptotics of singular values for $[(-\Delta_\theta)^{\frac{\epsilon}{2}},M_x]$. For this purpose, we extend the Cwikel estimates and the required asymptotics of singular values to arbitrary real antisymmetric matrices, and we also establish a systematic approximation theory of tempered distributions on quantum Euclidean spaces.
item.dc:creator: Changbao Pang, Maofa Wang, Hao Zhang

item.title: Quasinilpotency of commutators under a weakened Kleinecke--Shirokov condition
item.description: arXiv:2611.06423v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Kramar and Kramar Fijav\v{z} proved that a commutator $Y=AB-BA$ of two complex square matrices is nilpotent whenever $Y$ commutes with an iterated commutator $\delta_Y^{k}(A)$, where $\delta_Y(T)=YT-TY$, and asked whether this result can be generalized to bounded operators on infinite-dimensional spaces. We show that for $k\geq 2$ such a commutator need not be quasinilpotent. On the other hand, for every $k$ it is quasinilpotent whenever it is compact, or more generally whenever it is a Riesz operator or $AY-YA$ is compact. Moreover, its Riesz projection at any non-zero isolated point of its spectrum always has infinite rank.
item.dc:creator: Hranislav Stankovi\'c

item.title: Szeg\H{o} quasiforms: a Schottky-scheme construction for vertex operator superalgebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.06446v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the half weight ($N=\half$) analogue of the Bers quasiform on a Schottky group $\Gamma$ of genus $g$: the Poincar\'e series $S_\eps(x,y)=\sum_{\gt\in\Gt}j(\gt,x)/(\gamma x-y)\,(dx\,dy)^{1/2}$ over a lift $\Gt\subset\mathrm{SL}_2(\C)$ of $\Gamma$. The $\Ng:=2^{g}$ lifts give $\Ng$ trivial $\alpha$-holonomy even spin structures $\Lg$. The remaining $2^{2g}-\Ng$ spin structures are not treated in this paper. We prove, on an open set (H) of Schottky parameters and more generally whenever the critical exponent of $\Gamma$ is below $\half$ (any genus $g\ge 1$) the following: absolute and locally uniform convergence on $\Omega_0\times\Omega_0$, where $\Omega_0$ is the full region of discontinuity including the point $\infty$ (treated in homogeneous coordinates); invariance without Eichler-type defect; skew-symmetry; a simple pole on the diagonal as the only singularity; $H^0(\Sg,\Lg)=0$; and hence identification of $S_\eps$ with the Szeg\H{o} kernel of $\Lg$. At genus one the kernel is computed explicitly and the relations between lifts and theta characteristics are determined. We further prove that the diagonal coefficient defines a projective connection that differs from the Bergman projective connection by a quadratic differential constructed from $\theta[\delta](0)$, a residue-reconstruction formula for half-differentials with poles of any order, an expansion in the Schottky multipliers, and a formula for the free fermion stress tensor.
item.dc:creator: A. Zuevsky

item.title: Nonisomorphic separable Banach spaces at Lipschitz distance one
item.description: arXiv:2611.06493v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct nonisomorphic separable real Banach spaces whose multiplicative Lipschitz distance is one. Building on OpenAI's graph-space construction, we arrange two sequences of graph spaces into countably many blocks and form two spaces that differ by a single additional block. This block distinguishes their linear structures: one space contains a complemented copy of $\ell_1(c_0(\ell_2))$, whereas the other does not. By mapping the additional block to increasingly late positions and rearranging the remaining blocks, we obtain homeomorphisms whose Lipschitz constants and those of their inverses tend to one, while both spaces and their norms remain unchanged.
item.dc:creator: Ryotaro Tanaka

item.title: Real alternative Daugavet property without Daugavet property in a separable complex Banach space
item.description: arXiv:2611.06532v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a separable complex Banach space whose underlying real space has the alternative Daugavet property, although the complex space fails the Daugavet property, thereby answering an open question posed by Kadets, Martin, and Paya in 2006.
item.dc:creator: Jinghao Huang, Ran Xu

item.title: Dual Banach spaces with AP but without BAP
item.description: arXiv:2611.06579v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give negative answers to the AP-to-BAP and BAP-to-MAP questions for dual Banach spaces. More precisely, there is a separable Banach space $V$ with the metric approximation property (MAP) such that $V^*$ has the approximation property (AP) but no bounded approximation property (BAP). There is also a separable MAP space $X$, isomorphic to $\ell_1$, whose dual has BAP but no MAP. This resolves a longstanding open question explicitly stated in \cite{Oja2010}. The constructions rely on a finitely generated group without Property A and a quantitative estimate for optimal bounded approximation constants of projective tensor products.
item.dc:creator: Longfa Sun, Zhenguo Wei, Zhendong Xu, Hao Zhang

item.title: Spectral and mapping properties of the inverse Ornstein--Uhlenbeck operator
item.description: arXiv:2611.06826v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the spectral and boundedness properties of the inverse Ornstein--Uhlenbeck operator $\mathcal{A}^{Q,B}$ and its associated semigroup in $L^p$ spaces with respect to the inverse Gaussian measure. We establish strong continuity and contractivity of this semigroup in $L^p$ for $p \in [1, \infty)$, and obtain a complete characterization of the spectrum of $\mathcal{A}^{Q,B}$. For $p \in (1, \infty)$, the spectrum is independent of $p$, consists entirely of eigenvalues and exhibits a spectral gap. For $p=1$, the spectrum is instead the left half-plane. Furthermore, we discuss ultracontractivity and hypercontractivity properties of the semigroup.
item.dc:creator: Tommaso Bruno, Valentina Casarino, Paolo Ciatti, Peter Sj\"ogren

item.title: Independent Backward Preimages and Algebraic Radial Decompositions of Operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.06831v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $T\in\mathcal{B}(X)$, where $X$ is a complex Banach space. We introduce the spaces $\mathcal{I}_s(T)$, defined by independently chosen preimages under the powers of $T$ with exponential growth bounds, and study algebraic radial decompositions involving $\mathcal{H}_r(T)$, $\mathcal{K}_s(T)$, and $\mathcal{I}_s(T)$. We prove that every algebraic decomposition $X=\mathcal{H}_r(T)\oplus\mathcal{I}_s(T)$ is topological and that $\mathcal{I}_s(T)=\mathcal{K}_s(T)$. This removes the closedness assumption in the radial decomposition theorem of Koliha and Poon. We also prove that, for $0\leq a\leq b$, the closedness of $\mathcal{I}_b(T)$ and $\mathcal{H}_a(T)+\mathcal{I}_b(T)$ implies $\mathcal{I}_b(T)=\mathcal{K}_b(T)$. We establish finite-defect and circular spectral criteria and characterize the Cantor--Bendixson derivatives of the spectrum, Browder spectrum, and Drazin spectrum in terms of radial decompositions and quotient restrictions. As applications, we obtain new characterizations of generalized Drazin, generalized Drazin--Riesz, generalized Drazin--meromorphic, and $g_z$-invertible operators in terms of radial subspaces.
item.dc:creator: Zakariae Aznay, Fadil Chabbabi, Hassan Zariouh

item.title: One-third H\"older stability of optimal transport maps from log-concave sources
item.description:
arXiv:2611.05534v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove quantitative stability of quadratic optimal transport maps from arbitrary log-concave sources to bounded targets. If the source $ho$ is isotropic on $\mathbb R^d$ and the targets $\mu$, $
u$ are supported in a common ball of radius $R$, their Brenier maps satisfy \[ \lVert T_\mu-T_
uVert_{L^2(ho)} \leqslant 17d^{2/3}R^{2/3}W_2(\mu,
u)^{1/3}. \] The one-third exponent is optimal for $d\geqslant2$. The proof combines a linear stability estimate for Brenier potentials in a weighted norm with a matching weighted reverse Poincar'e inequality. The weight is chosen in terms of the negative log-density of the source to account for its tails. We also show that the best dimensional constant in map stability is at least of order $d^{1/3}$.
item.dc:creator: Songbo Wang, Xiaozhen Wang

item.title: Sharp Hausdorff--Young inequalities for some locally compact quantum groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.05863v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we show that the usual Hausdorff--Young inequalities for locally compact quantum groups such as the quantum \(E_q(2)\), the real quantum \(az+b\), and the extended quantum \(SU_q(1,1)\), where \(0<q<1\), are sharp. Moreover, there are no group-like projections with finite Haar weight in these locally compact quantum groups. We obtain a sharp Hausdorff--Young inequality for Kahng's skew-matrix quantum groups; the optimal constant is strictly less than one for \(1<p<2\); at \(p=2\), Plancherel gives equality, and these quantum groups have no nonzero group-like projections with finite Haar weight.
item.dc:creator: Jinsong Wu, Fulin Yang

item.title: The Kato square root property for fractional elliptic operators in divergence form
item.description:
arXiv:2611.06391v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish the Kato square root property for fractional elliptic operators $L = -\operatorname{div}^\alpha(\mu 
abla^\alpha \cdot)$ of order $2\alpha \in (0,2)$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$, built from the Riesz fractional gradient and divergence, with bounded, measurable and uniformly elliptic complex coefficients $\mu$. More precisely, we show that the domain of $L^{1/2}$ coincides with the distributional fractional Sobolev space $\mathrm{S}^{\alpha,2}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and that $\|L^{1/2} u\|_{\mathrm{L}^2} \simeq \|
abla^\alpha u\|_{\mathrm{L}^2}$, with constants that are locally uniform in $\alpha$. As a consequence, we recover the Kato square root property for elliptic operators $-\operatorname{div}(\mu
abla\cdot)$ in the limit $\alpha 	o 1$, and we obtain continuity of the square root with respect to the parameter $\alpha$. The proof follows the second-order approach to the Kato problem. Its two new ingredients are nonlocal off-diagonal estimates of polynomial order for the resolvents of $L$, and a construction of $T(b)$-test functions that circumvents the nonlocality of $
abla^\alpha$ by factorizing it through Riesz potentials.
item.dc:creator: Luca Haardt

item.title: Near-Riesz and pseudo-Riesz bases of Hilbert C*-modules and semi-C*-Fredholm operators
item.description: arXiv:2606.16597v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Several useful concepts of almost frames or Riesz bases of Hilbert spaces gave us the motivation to review the theory of C*-module frames and C*-module Riesz bases for Hilbert C*-modules, searching for similar useful structures. We give a survey of the background in C*-module frame theory, summarizing and particularly extending or correcting earlier results. The concepts of near-Riesz bases, pseudo-frames, pseudo-Riesz sequences, and pseudo Riesz bases of Hilbert C*-modules are introduced and equivalently related to (semi-)C*-Fredholm properties of their synthesis operators. The notion of the excess of a C*-module frame is introduced, taking values in related C* algebras. Indicators for possible erasures of frame elements are described with the aim to preserve robustness of frames. Introducing a new notion of pseudo-Riesz-Weyl sequences in the standard Hilbert C*-module $l_2(A)$ we reverse the found correspondence by assuming the associated synthesis operator of a Bessel sequence to be (upper semi-)C*-Weyl. Furthermore, we deduce from the invariance of (upper semi-)C*-Fredholm and C*-Riesz-Weyl properties of synthesis operators with respect to ''compact'' perturbations the perturbation invariance of the respective classes of module Bessel sequences.
item.dc:creator: Michael Frank, Stefan Ivkovic

item.title: Single commutators in Schatten ideals
item.description: arXiv:2610.27024v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $r>2$ and let $p,q\in(0,\infty)$ satisfy $r^{-1}=p^{-1}+q^{-1}$. We prove that every $T\in \mathcal{S}_r(\mathcal H)$ is a single commutator $T=[A,B]$ with $A\in \mathcal{S}_p(\mathcal H)$ and $B\in \mathcal{S}_q(\mathcal H)$. Combined with L. G. Brown's theorem for $1 \leq r \leq 2$, this completely resolves the Pearcy--Topping problem for Schatten ideals. We also obtain simultaneous operator and Schatten norm bounds for the factors.
item.dc:creator: Zhichao Liu, Shanshan Yang

item.title: Perturbations of Truncated Toeplitz operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.40295v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the structure of kernels of finite-rank perturbations of truncated Toeplitz operators. By realizing a perturbed truncated Toeplitz operator on a model space as a suitable matrix-valued truncated Toeplitz operator on an enlarged model space, we identify its kernel with a coordinate projection of the kernel of an associated block Toeplitz operator. This realization enables us to transfer the nearly $S^*$-invariant structure of Toeplitz kernels to the perturbed truncated setting. More precisely, for a perturbation of rank at most $n$, we show that the kernel of the perturbed truncated Toeplitz operator is nearly $S^*$-invariant with defect at most $2n+1$. We then extend the method to truncated Toeplitz operators on multiband spaces. In this setting, a perturbation of rank at most $n$ again preserves the finite-defect nearly $S^*$-invariant structure of the kernel, with the explicit upper bound $2n+2$ for the defect.
item.dc:creator: Arup Chattopadhyay, Arshad Khan

item.title: The extension of traces for Sobolev mappings between manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2403.18738v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The compact Riemannian manifolds $\mathcal{M}$ and $\mathcal{N}$ for which the trace operator from the first-order Sobolev space of mappings $\smash{\dot{W}}^{1, p} (\mathcal{M}, \mathcal{N})$ to the fractional Sobolev-Slobodecki\u{\i} space $\smash{\smash{\dot{W}}^{1 - 1/p, p}} (\partial \mathcal{M}, \mathcal{N})$ is surjective when $1 < p < \dim \mathcal{M}$ are characterised. The traces are extended using a new construction which can be carried out assuming the absence of the known topological and analytical obstructions. When $p \ge \dim \mathcal{M}$ the same construction provides a Sobolev extension with linear estimates for maps that have a continuous extension, provided that the known analytical obstructions to such a control are not present.
item.dc:creator: Jean Van Schaftingen

item.title: On the Existence, Smoothness, and Order-Two Entire Extension of the Navier-Stokes Equations in Critical Fourier-Besov Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2405.07929v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish global existence, smoothness, and physical energy bounds for solutions to the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations on $\mathbb{R}^d$ ($d \ge 3$) under a scaling-critical smallness condition in the homogeneous Fourier-Besov spaces $\mathscr{X}_p(\mathbb{R}^d)$, defined as the weak space $F \dot{B}^{\frac{d}{p'}-1}_{p,\infty}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ for $1 < p \le \infty$ and $F \dot{B}^{-1}_{1,1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ at the endpoint $p = 1$. By combining the nonassociative algebra of Riesz convolutions and spaces of functions dominated by Fourier-Caloric flows $\mathscr{V}(\lambda)$ with a Littlewood-Paley dyadic atomic decomposition, we prove that the Catalan Picard series converges globally whenever $\|\widehat{u^0}\|_{\mathscr{X}_p(\mathbb{R}^d)} < C\nu$. This threshold reaches the sharp boundary of well-posedness prior to norm inflation, strictly improves upon the classical Fujita-Kato $\dot{H}^{\frac{d}{2}-1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ condition, and admits explicit multiscale Schwartz initial data with arbitrarily large $\dot{H}^{\frac{d}{2}-1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and $H^k(\mathbb{R}^d)$ norms. Furthermore, we demonstrate that for positive times, the velocity and pressure fields admit an analytic extension to the complex domain $\mathbb{C}^d$, forming a smooth curve of entire vector fields of order two. Finally, for arbitrary initial data outside the critical ball, we employ fractional Riesz convolutions $*_\alpha$ ($0 < \alpha < 1$) to derive an explicit lower bound $T_{\max}(u^0) > 0$ on the lifespan of smooth, order-two entire solutions, establishing a sharp dichotomy between global continuation via viscous re-entry into the critical ball and a scaling-invariant lower blow-up rate.
item.dc:creator: Brian David Vasquez Campos

item.title: Variational formulae for entropy-like functionals for states in von Neumann algebras
item.description: arXiv:2510.07605v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The paper presents variational formulae for entropy-like functionals, including Segal and R\'enyi entropies, for normal states on semifinite von Neumann algebras. The considered functionals are of the form $\tau(f(h))$ where $\tau$ is a normal faithful semifinite trace on this algebra, $h$ is a positive selfadjoint operator from $L^1(\mathscr{M},\tau)$, and $f$ is an appropriate convex or concave function. The results cover both finite and semifinite algebras, and the obtained formulae generalise known results, in particular, those concerning relative entropy. Moreover, the connection between quantum entropies and the structure of abelian subalgebras is highlighted, providing new interpretations in the context of quantum information theory.
item.dc:creator: Andrzej {\L}uczak, Hanna Pods\k{e}dkowska, Rafa{\l} Wieczorek

item.title: Dirac solitons in one-dimensional nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations
item.description: arXiv:2512.24089v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper we study a family of one-dimensional stationary cubic nonlinear Schr\"odinger (NLS) equations with periodic potentials and linear part displaying Dirac points in the dispersion relation. By introducing a suitable periodic perturbation, one can open a spectral gap around the Dirac-point energy. This allows to construct standing waves of the NLS equation whose leading-order profile is a modulation of Bloch waves by means of the components of a spinor solving an appropriate cubic nonlinear Dirac (NLD) equation. We refer to these solutions as Dirac solitons. Our analysis thus provides a rigorous justification for the use of the NLD equation as an effective model for the original NLS equation.
item.dc:creator: William Borrelli, Elena Danesi, Simone Dovetta, Lorenzo Tentarelli

item.title: Phase Retrievability of Super Operators and Measurements
item.description: arXiv:2607.26474v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We continue the study of Phase Retrieval in the Quantum Information setting in the style of \cite{liu2023phase}, in a manner which is more general in two primary ways: (a) Instead of only pure states we consider also states (and positive semidefinite operators) of bounded rank, as is done in Quantum Tomography; (b) We consider general super operators instead of only quantum channels. We show that in order to have phase retrieval with respect to positive semidefinite operators of bounded rank, it suffices to discriminate between perfectly distinguishable pairs (i.e. those with orthogonal supports). From this we prove that phase retrievability is always Lipschitz stable with respect to the trace norm, and then we use the Fuchs-van de Graaf inequalities to deduce stability with respect to the Bures--Wasserstein distance (thus generalizing the known stability results for phase retrieval in Frame Theory). For Hermitian-preserving super operators taking values in block-diagonal matrices, we characterize phase retrievability in terms of conditions inspired by the classical complement property from Frame Theory.
item.dc:creator: Javier Alejandro Ch\'avez-Dom\'inguez, Jeremiah Ifeanyi Isu

item.title: Distance-Weighted Norm Equivalences for Analytic Functions on John Domains
item.description: arXiv:2608.23940v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb C$ be a bounded John domain and set $\delta(z)=\text{dist}(z,\partial\Omega)$. For $1<p<\infty$ and $\alpha>\text{dim}_A(\partial\Omega)-2$, we establish a norm equivalence between $\int_\Omega |g|^p\delta^\alpha\,dA$ and $\int_\Omega |g'|^p\delta^{\alpha+p}\,dA$ for analytic functions $g$ on $\Omega$, with a point-evaluation term fixing the additive constant. The estimate of the derivative term is local and holds on every proper planar domain, whereas the converse follows from a distance-weighted Poincar\'e inequality on John domains. Taking $\alpha=mp-2$ yields the corresponding comparison between the $m$-th and $(m+1)$-st derivatives. For $m\ge2$ the boundary-dimension condition is automatic, so the only dimension-sensitive case is the comparison between $\int_\Omega |f'|^p\delta^{p-2}\,dA$ and $\int_\Omega |f''|^p\delta^{2p-2}\,dA$ when $1<p<2$. We show that this restriction is sharp within the class of quasidisks by using self-similar Rohde snowflakes. We also construct, for every $s>1$, an inward-cusp $s$-John domain on which the comparison fails, showing that the ordinary John condition cannot in general be weakened.
item.dc:creator: Katsuhiko Matsuzaki, Huaying Wei

item.title: Classification of bipartite observables II: NIP observables and the Todorcevic trichotomy
item.description: arXiv:2610.12908v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This is the second paper in a series that reads the dividing lines of Shelah's classification theory as properties of bipartite quantum observables. For an observable of two independently prepared systems, Alice's and Bob's, we study its idealized responses: the expectation values of Alice's limiting preparations, as functions of Bob's preparations, which serve as probes, with Bob's system idealized first. We show that the observable is NIP, that is, no sequence of Alice's preparations lets Bob's probes realize every finite pattern of high and low values at a fixed positive gap, exactly when all idealized responses are of the first Baire class, pointwise limits of sequences of continuous functions; they then form a separable Rosenthal compactum. Because Alice can mix preparations, this compactum is convex, and hereditary separability forces it to be metrizable, so that NIP observables occupy three of the four topological classes defined by metrizability and Todor\v{c}evi\'c's trichotomy. Comparisons of photon numbers, of positions and of events in spacetime realize these three classes, and trees of preparations realize the seven minimal families of the Argyros--Dodos--Kanellopoulos heptachotomy. For the ferromagnetic transverse-field Ising model at positive temperature, the finite-volume magnetizations with offset longitudinal fields form a stable family when the spontaneous magnetization vanishes, and a family whose closure is first countable but not hereditarily separable when it does not.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Due\~nez, Jos\'e Iovino
